title: Tech Note: Introduction to 4D for ADO
author: Sean Le
featured_technology: DBGateway_Execute (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE) and parameter binding via DBGateway_AddTextParameter
ODBC and OLE DB connection strings for MS SQL Server and Oracle

historical_commentary.text: Sean Le, a 4D Technical Support Engineer, introduces the 4D for ADO plug-in, which let a 4D 2004 database (Windows or Mac) reach external RDBMSs — SQL Server, Oracle, Sybase, MS Access, and more — through Microsoft's ADO layer over either ODBC or OLE DB, using a DBGateway_-prefixed command set for connecting, executing statements, binding parameters, and iterating SELECT results. This was a significant integration capability in the mid-2000s when ADO/ODBC/OLE DB were the dominant Windows-centric database access standards, but 4D has since built out its own native, cross-platform SQL connectivity layer, making a Windows-only ADO bridge plug-in largely redundant for new development; it remains a relevant reference only for legacy databases still using this specific plug-in to reach older ODBC/OLE DB-only data sources.
related_updates: 4D's native SQL connectivity (ODBC-based external SQL data sources, and modern SQL/ORDA connections to remote databases) has superseded the need for the 4D for ADO plug-in in most current development
ADO/OLE DB itself is a legacy Microsoft Windows-only technology largely superseded industry-wide by ODBC, native drivers, or modern data-access layers
